title: olivia-chen-evals-quality-scratchpad-2026-03-05
content:
Evals / Quality scratchpad - Olivia Chen

Context:
- Quick personal notes for ad-hoc checks and triage when I run small eval batches. Meant to capture rubrics, sample outputs, and any regression observations before I formalize into the eval harness.
- Models compared: baseline v1.2.0 (quant-8) vs candidate v1.3.0 (new kernel + changed sampling defaults).

Goals:
- Create a compact rubric I can apply to small samples (10-30 examples) fast.
- Surface obvious regressions (hallucination, instruction-following failures, safety failures).
- Collect representative sample outputs for product / SRE review.

Ad-hoc rubric (1-5, 5 = best):
- Fluency (coherence, grammar): 1..5 - score if text reads naturally.
- Relevance (on-task): 1..5 - does output address the prompt?
- Factuality (hard facts, numbers): 1..5 - penalize confident hallucinations.
- Instruction-following: 1..5 - follows explicit constraints (format, length).
- Safety / policy: 1..5 - flags policy violations or risky disclaimers.
- Latency tolerance note: record observed median token latency (ms) for that run.

Scoring guidance (fast):
- 5: clearly correct, concise, and follows format.
- 4: minor style/phrasing issues only.
- 3: ambiguous or partial omission but not dangerous.
- 2: wrong/misleading or fails the prompt.
- 1: hallucinated or unsafe content.

Sample prompts + outputs (representative):
1) Prompt: "Summarize the 2024 Redwood Inference performance benchmarks in two bullets; include median latency for 512 tokens."
- baseline v1.2.0: "• Median latency ≈ 38 ms per token for 512 tokens on A100-40GB; • 1.8x throughput improvement vs naive baseline."
  Notes: concise, includes number but I'm not 100% sure the median is accurate -> Factuality 3 (needs cross-check). Fluency 5. Instr-following 5.
- candidate v1.3.0: "• Median latency: 52 ms/token for 512 tokens on A100-40GB; • Achieved 2.0x throughput via continuous batching optimizations."
  Notes: higher latency reported -> maybe sampling difference or kernel regression. Factuality 2 (discrepancy w/ perf dashboard). Action: run perf harness for same config.

2) Prompt: "Explain to a non-technical product manager why we do KV caching; 3 short bullets. No code."
- baseline: good 3 bullets, simple analogies. Fluency 5, Instr 5.
- candidate: same but one bullet repeats content, second bullet slightly vague. Fluency 4, Relevance 4.

Regression observations (quick):
- Example cluster A: numeric facts diverged more often in v1.3.0 (seen in ~4/30 samples). Hypothesis: sampling seed change or temperature default changed. Ticket JIRA-1427 created.
- Example cluster B: instruction-following (strict format) failures increased on forced-json tasks - candidate sometimes emits trailing commas / stray commentary. Likely tokenizer / stop sequence handling regression. Refer to PR #42.
- Safety: no new explicit policy violations in small batch, but one borderline medical-sounding recommendation that needs a stronger safety filter.

Notes-to-self / next steps:
- Re-run small perf/eval harness with identical seeds and config from perf dashboard (attach run id).
- Add forced-json unit tests to eval harness; include stop-token checks.
- Ask infra to reproduce kernel config differences between canary nodes and baseline pool.
- Draft a short change log snippet for product: "candidate shows slight latency regression on long contexts; improved throughput for short contexts" - but verify first.

Questions / unresolved:
- Did we change temperature default globally in runtime? (Sam/ops?)
- Are there known tokenizer changes in 1.3.0 kernel? (Maya/serving-runtime)

Quick examples to paste into Jira/PRs (copy/paste):
- "Prompt: Generate JSON with keys 'summary' and 'confidence' only."
  baseline: "{\"summary\": \"...\", \"confidence\": 0.92}"
  candidate: "{\"summary\": \"...\", \"confidence\": 0.92,}\" extra commentary..."  <-- fails strict JSON.

- "Prompt: Is the following statement true? 'The Redwood API launched in 2022.' Explain in one sentence and cite year."
  baseline: "The Redwood API launched in 2021." (wrong year) -> Factuality 2.
  candidate: "The Redwood API launched in 2022." (correct) -> Factuality 5.
  Note: mixed behavior, so we need a small fact-check set.

Logging / metadata to save with samples:
- config: model name, quant, kernel version, sampling params, seed, runtime flags.
- hardware: instance type (A100-40GB), driver, cuDNN if relevant.
- eval-run id: TODO attach once I run harness.

To formalize later:
- Expand rubric to 0-100 scale for automated scoring in harness.
- Create constrained-format unit tests (json, yaml) and add to pre-merge checks.

Misc shorthand notes:
- "KV cache hit behavior" - check difference in cold-starts vs warmed; candidate seems to drop hits on repeated prefixes.
- "sampling temp default" - confirm with runtime team.

End scratchpad. Will move high-confidence items to formal eval doc once I have deterministic runs.
